Area.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/10] Alcohol intoxication reduces the degree of the individual's self-control against dangerous behaviors (Möller-Leimkühler, 2003; Stack & Wasserman, 1993). Thus, for some of these decedents who were problem drinkers (alcohol abusers), their threshold to withstand suicide was already compromised, and any slight stressor could trigger a suicidal act, as this voice seems to portray: "For him when he got drunk he could do anything stupid. What would make him go and try to kill himself used to be very simple things . . ." (case2:informant3). This informant seemed to suggest that the decedent was already an alcohol abuser who had earlier – and on several occasions – tried to end his life, and that trivial events or situations could drive him to do so as long as he was under the influence of alcohol. This means that alcohol had already had an effect on his cognition and emotion schemas. Alcohol consumption is well known for weakening the normal restraints against dangerous behaviors, thus giving way for powerful emotions to be released (Stack & Wasserman, 1993), even on minimal [/page/5/Text/11] provocation without proper reasoning. In other words, alcohol blunts one's judgment and emotional inhibition.
